AnalyzerError.description:
An analyzer whose ``analyze()`` raised or returned something unusable
(#220). The scan carries on without it; this records the gap.
AnalyzerError.title: AnalyzerError

Anomaly.description:
A within-repo consistency outlier — the odd-one-out in a peer group (#78).

Emitted by the `anomalies` analyzer. Rather than matching a known-bad
signature, it flags a route that deviates from the norm its siblings
establish: peers in the same resource cohort carry an auth/validation
signal (or are read-only) and this one doesn't. The bigger and more
consistent the peer group, the more likely the deviation is a mistake —
so `confidence` scales with `consistent_peers`.

`invariant_violation` (#149a) is the mined-invariant variant: the cohort
is not a route-path prefix but the set of handlers that reach the same
dangerous sink kind, and the norm they establish is a *behavioural*
invariant ("guard the request before the sink") rather than a static
signal. When set, `invariant` states the mined rule as evidence.
Anomaly.title: Anomaly

AppSurfaceIssue.description:
A mobile/desktop app attack-surface issue emitted by a platform plugin
(#188, #190): the Apple analyzers (Swift, Objective-C) report App Transport
Security exceptions, custom URL-scheme handlers, weakening entitlements,
WKWebView script built from strings, secrets in UserDefaults or on the
pasteboard, unvalidated XPC peers, and classes, selectors or libraries
resolved from runtime strings. Native format-string and command-exec
constructs are `CodeWeakness` kinds shared with the C/C++ plugins.

Core owns the findings: one aggregated finding per kind (rule id = the
kind, dashed), at the most severe instance's severity. Like the other
issue families, every instance is a positively-present construct, never
an absence.

``kind`` is one of ``APP_SURFACE_ISSUE_KINDS`` but typed ``str``, so a
plugin built against a newer core still validates: core drops records
with a kind it doesn't know (noted under ``analyzer_errors``) and keeps
the rest of the plugin's result.
AppSurfaceIssue.title: AppSurfaceIssue

AttackChain.description: Steps ordered so each step's `requires` is met by `start` or an earlier step.
AttackChain.title: AttackChain

AttackTechnique.description: Reference to a MITRE ATT&CK technique (Enterprise matrix).
AttackTechnique.title: AttackTechnique

BolaCandidate.description:
A route that may be missing object-level authorization (#69).

Emitted by the authz analyzer when a route takes a resource
identifier and reaches a datastore, but no ownership/authorization
check is visible near the handler. Heuristic — the ownership-marker
scan is the main false-positive reducer; confidence stays honest.
BolaCandidate.title: BolaCandidate

ChainStep.description: One finding as a capability transition: `requires` → `grants`.
ChainStep.title: ChainStep

CloudMisconfig.description:
A cloud, IaC or container-runtime misconfiguration (terraform#4, iac#1).

Emitted by IaC plugins (Terraform, Kubernetes / Helm, compose,
Dockerfile). Like the other issue families, each one is a
positively-present setting (or a documented insecure default that the
file leaves in place) at a file and line. Core turns each `kind` into
findings, one per (kind, severity) tier, so a low `/var/log` mount never
inherits the severity of a `docker.sock` mount of the same kind.

- `kind`: one of `CLOUD_MISCONFIG_KINDS`. Typed `str` so a plugin built
  against a newer core still validates here; core drops records with a
  kind it doesn't know (noted under `analyzer_errors`) and keeps the rest
  of the plugin's result.
- `resource`: what the setting belongs to, e.g. `aws_eks_cluster.main`,
  `Deployment/web container app`, `module.vpc`.
- `platform`: one of `CLOUD_MISCONFIG_PLATFORMS`.
- `context`: how the resource is instantiated — `for_each`/`count`,
  the calling module of a local module, a Helm template.
- `escalation_path`: what an attacker gets from it, in one line, e.g.
  `hostPath / → node root → kubelet credentials`.

The free-text fields are redacted, folded to one line and capped.
CloudMisconfig.title: CloudMisconfig

CodeWeakness.description:
A novel vulnerability-class weakness in source (#77).

Emitted by the built-in `weaknesses` finder — bug classes beyond the
taint/crypto/web-hardening families, detected from concrete risky
constructs (not absence).
CodeWeakness.title: CodeWeakness

CryptoWeakness.description:
An insecure-cryptography or weak-randomness usage (#70).

Emitted by the built-in crypto finder. Heuristic and regex-based;
the noisy families (weak hash, insecure RNG) are gated on a
security-context identifier to keep precision high.
CryptoWeakness.title: CryptoWeakness

DependencyHint.description:
A single third-party dependency declared in a manifest or lockfile.

Manifests (#48) carry version *ranges* verbatim (``^4.16.0``, ``>=2,<3``,
``latest``) and only direct dependencies. Lockfiles (#143) carry *exact*
resolved versions and the full transitive tree — those hints set
``resolved=True`` and populate ``direct`` / ``via``.
DependencyHint.title: DependencyHint

ExploitabilityFactor.description:
One named, signed contribution to an exploitability score (#79).

Kept explicit so every score is explainable — the report shows exactly
which signals raised (or, at 0 points, notably did not raise) the number.
ExploitabilityFactor.title: ExploitabilityFactor

ExploitabilityScore.description:
A fused 'exploitable now' score for one route→sink combination (#79).

Deterministic: the same scan always yields the same score, and `factors`
sums (before the 0–100 clamp) to `raw_score`, so nothing is hidden.
ExploitabilityScore.title: ExploitabilityScore

FindingLocation.description:
A file (and line, when known) a finding applies to (#214). Carried
structurally so SARIF, suppression and diffing don't have to parse
evidence prose.
FindingLocation.title: FindingLocation

FindingTaxonomy.description:
Standard ids for a finding's rule (#250), looked up by `rule_id` in
`attackmap.taxonomy` — never inferred from title or evidence text.
FindingTaxonomy.title: FindingTaxonomy

LogicFlawCandidate.description:
A business-logic or race-condition lead on a mutating route (#245):
`check_then_act` (a balance-like `field` checked, then written, with no
lock) or `idempotency_gap` (a redeem/checkout/transfer POST with no
idempotency, uniqueness or rate-limit signal). Always needs human review.
LogicFlawCandidate.title: LogicFlawCandidate

SecretHistoryHit.description:
A hard-coded secret found in git history (#252, ``--secrets-history``).

``name`` is the masked value; ``introduced_in`` is the oldest scanned
commit that added it; ``still_in_head`` is False when a later commit
removed it from the file (it remains in every clone's history).
SecretHistoryHit.title: SecretHistoryHit

SupplyChainIssue.description:
A dependency supply-chain risk beyond CVEs (#247).

Emitted by the built-in, offline ``supply_chain`` pass over manifests,
lockfiles and package-manager configs: dependency confusion, typosquat
candidates, mutable VCS/URL dependencies, install scripts, unlocked
manifests and insecure registries.
SupplyChainIssue.title: SupplyChainIssue

TaintChain.description:
Cross-file data-flow evidence: a route reaches a sink via imports.

Emitted by the lite taint analyzer (see #45). Each entry names the
starting route, the sink kind and location, and the chain of files
the import-walk traversed. Confidence encodes that import-edge is a
heuristic proxy for call-edge — real dispatch may not hit the sink.
TaintChain.title: TaintChain

TaintFlowStep.description:
One step of an intra-procedural flow (#239): where the tainted value
came from, each assignment it passed through, any sanitizer/guard bound to
it, and the sink. Rendered as SARIF ``codeFlows``. ``evidence_text`` is
the code at that step (redacted like other evidence).
TaintFlowStep.title: TaintFlowStep

Vulnerability.description:
A known CVE / advisory affecting a resolved dependency (#60).

One entry per (dep × advisory). ``package_version`` is the concrete
lower-bound the CVE lookup resolved from the manifest spec — it may
differ from the DependencyHint's raw ``version`` string.
Vulnerability.title: Vulnerability

WebHardeningIssue.description:
A web-hardening misconfiguration (#71).

Emitted by the built-in web-hardening finder. Detects
positively-present misconfigurations (wildcard CORS with credentials,
explicit CSRF disable, insecure cookie flags, unsafe-inline/eval CSP,
debug enabled) rather than hard-to-judge absences.
WebHardeningIssue.title: WebHardeningIssue

WebhookVerification.description:
How a webhook handler authenticates the events it receives (#243, part B).

``verified``: a provider SDK verifier, or an HMAC checked with a
constant-time compare (and, for schemes that sign a timestamp, a freshness
check). ``weak_compare``: an HMAC compared with ``==``. ``no_replay_guard``:
a timestamped scheme whose timestamp is never checked. ``absent``: nothing
that verifies the payload. ``unknown``: the handler couldn't be read, or it
hands the signature to code we couldn't follow.
WebhookVerification.title: WebhookVerification

WorkflowIssue.description:
A CI-workflow security issue in a GitHub Actions file (#142).

Emitted by the built-in workflow scanner over ``.github/workflows/*.yml``.
Every issue is a positively-present misconfiguration (an unpinned action,
an untrusted-code checkout under ``pull_request_target``, a secret or an
attacker-controlled context interpolated into a shell step, ``write-all``
permissions, a self-hosted runner on a PR trigger) — a hardened workflow
produces nothing.
WorkflowIssue.title: WorkflowIssue
